info.title: Chat API

post.description:
Returns a short-lived `token` (access) and a long-lived `refreshToken`.
Store both; when the access token expires, call `POST /api/auth/refresh`
instead of asking for the password again.

Send the session's `refreshToken` in the body — that is what actually gets revoked.
Without it the server has nothing to invalidate and the session stays alive until
it expires.
            
Idempotent: an unknown or already-revoked token also returns 200, so the endpoint
cannot be used to find out which tokens exist. The access token keeps working until
it expires (minutes) — discard it client-side.
post.summary: Log out of the current session.

post.description:
Revokes all refresh tokens of the current user — use it after a password change or
when a device is lost. Already-issued access tokens stay valid until they expire.
post.summary: Log out of every session on all devices.

post.description:
Needs the current password. Every other sign-in of the user ends at once — their refresh
tokens stop working and their hub connections close; this device stays signed in. Access
tokens already issued to other devices work until they expire (minutes). Limited like
sign-in: 5 attempts a minute from one IP.
            
Errors: `400 WRONG_PASSWORD`, `400 PASSWORD_TOO_LONG`, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`
(new password shorter than 6), `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

Call this when the access token has expired (or is about to). The endpoint is
anonymous on purpose — the expired access token is not required, and not accepted
as proof of anything.
            
**Rotation:** every successful call invalidates the refresh token you sent and
returns a new one. Always persist the new value.
            
**Parallel refreshes are safe.** A token that was rotated less than 30 seconds ago
still works, so two requests racing after a 401 both succeed instead of logging the
user out. Replaying a token after that window is treated as theft and revokes every
session in that login's chain (`REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`).
            
Error codes: `INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `SESSION_REVOKED`,
`REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`, `USER_INACTIVE`, `USER_NOT_FOUND` — all as 401.
Any of them means the same thing for the client: show the login screen.
post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair.

post.description:
Registration signs the user in: the response carries the same access and
refresh tokens as `POST /api/auth/login`.

get.description:
Returns userId, username, and isValid flag.
Use this endpoint to check if the access token has expired or is malformed.
Unlike other endpoints, this one is anonymous so it can test tokens
that may already be expired or tampered with.
            
This says nothing about the refresh token or the session — a valid answer here
does not mean the session is still alive, and an invalid one does not mean the
user must log in again (try `POST /api/auth/refresh` first).
            
Sample request:
  GET /api/auth/validate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer {token}
get.summary: Validate whether a JWT access token is still valid.

get.description:
Case-insensitive. Only active users. Lookup by email is not supported on purpose:
an email address must not reveal whether its owner has an account.
get.summary: Get a user's ID by username.

get.description:
Intended for session restore: a client that kept the token but lost its local
user data (cache cleared, app reinstalled) can recover the same user fields
login/register returns, without asking for credentials again.
            
Returns userId, username, email and displayName — i.e. the login response
minus the token. Unlike `GET /api/users/{userId}` this includes the email,
since it is the caller's own data.
            
A 404 here means the token is valid but the account no longer exists —
the client should discard the token and show the login screen.
            
Sample request:
  GET /api/users/me
get.summary: Get the current user's own profile, resolved from the JWT.

patch.description:

             Errors: `400 INVALID_DISPLAY_NAME`.

Errors: `400 INVALID_AVATAR` (not a photo), `404 ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`.

put.description:
Only the fields given change. Answers with all settings; the caller's other devices get
`PrivacyUpdated`.
            
- `lastSeen` — who sees online and last seen. It works both ways: whoever hides theirs
  (`nobody`) does not see the others' either. Takes effect at once.
- `messages` — who may start a private chat; an existing chat keeps working.
- `groupAdd` — who may add the caller to groups.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_PRIVACY`.

post.description:
Returns one entry per requested user, including offline ones (`isOnline: false`).
IDs you share no chat with are silently omitted from the response.
At most 200 IDs per request; duplicates are collapsed.
            
Purpose: entering the chat list screen. Send the `companionId`s of the private
chats currently on screen and get their presence in one round-trip, instead of
relying on `UserOnlineChanged` events that fired while the app was closed.
            
Sample request:
  POST /api/users/status
  { "userIds": ["3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6"] }

Returns the user's ID, username and display name.
Email is not exposed — it is private to the account owner; use `GET /api/users/me`
for your own profile. Online status is not exposed here either — use

put.description:
In a private chat neither may write to the other (the caller gets `403 USER_BLOCKED`, the
blocked one `403 PRIVACY_RESTRICTED` — the same as for privacy settings, so a block is not
told). The blocked one cannot start a private chat with the caller or add them to groups, and
sees neither their online, last seen nor avatar. Takes effect at once; the caller's devices
get `BlockListChanged`. Blocking twice is not an error.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (oneself), `404 USER_NOT_FOUND`.

get.description:
Unlike `GET /api/users/status`, this always answers about the user you asked for:
`isOnline: false` is returned explicitly when they are offline.
            
Purpose: opening a chat screen. The client knows the companion's id and needs
their current presence right away, without waiting for a `UserOnlineChanged` event
that may have fired while the app was closed.
            
Visible only for users you share a chat with (and for yourself); anything else
returns 404, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe whether an account exists.
            
Sample request:
  GET /api/users/3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6/status

post.description:
The caller becomes its owner; `memberIds` (may be empty) become members. The group
opens with a system message "group created". Up to `Groups:MaxMembers` (500) members,
the owner included.
            
The body is the caller's `ChatListItemDto` (`type: "group"`). The members receive
`ChatCreated` with their own card; the caller's other devices learn of the group through
`/api/sync`.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_TITLE` (1–128 characters after trimming), `400 TOO_MANY_MEMBERS`,
`404 USER_NOT_FOUND` (a member does not exist or is deactivated), `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

get.description:
The same `ChatListItemDto` as `GET /api/chats`, newest activity first (a new
message, or creation). `nextCursor` — pass it as `cursor` for the next page; null —
the end. A chat that gets a message while paging moves to the top: keep the list up to date
from events, not by reloading pages.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_CURSOR`.

post.description:
The body is a full `ChatListItemDto` — the same shape as an entry of
`GET /api/chats` — so the client can insert the chat into its list
without a follow-up request. The companion fields describe the *other*
participant as seen by the caller.
            
The other participant receives the same chat over SignalR as a
`ChatCreated` event, built from their own point of view.

Create a private chat with another user.

post.description:
One per user, created on first call: `201` then, `200` afterwards, the same
`ChatListItemDto` as in `GET /api/chats` with `type: "saved"` and no
title or companion (the client names it). Everything works as in any chat: send,
forward into it, edit, delete, react. The caller's other devices learn about a new one
through `/api/sync` (`ChatCreated`).

get.description:
Searches the current user's chats.
For group chats: searches by chat title (ILIKE).
For private chats: searches by companion display name or username (ILIKE).

Use the optional `type` parameter to filter results:
- `type=group` — search only group chats
- `type=private` — search only private chats
- omit `type` — search both

Sample requests:
- GET /api/chats/search?q=team&type=group&limit=20
- GET /api/chats/search?q=alice&type=private&limit=20
- GET /api/chats/search?q=something&limit=20

parameters.description: Optional type filter: "group", "private", or empty for both.
parameters.name: type

get.summary: Search user's chats by query.

delete.description:
The owner only. The group and its history are gone for all members; they receive
`ChatDeleted`, and their connections stop getting the group's events.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`,
`429 RATE_LIMITED`.

get.summary: Get chat details

patch.description:
Only the given fields change. `title` — needs `changeInfo`; members get a system
message "title changed". `memberPermissions` — the owner or an admin with
`removeMembers`; only `sendMessages`, `sendMedia`, `addMembers`,
`changeInfo`, and a given field changes, an omitted one stays (`{ "sendMessages": false }`
makes the group read-only for members). Members' own overrides still win.
            
The body is the group's title and default permissions now; members receive `ChatUpdated`
with the same. No change — no event.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `400 INVALID_TITLE`, `400 INVALID_PERMISSIONS`,
`403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
patch.summary: Rename a group or change what its members may do by default.

put.description:
An archived chat is not in the main list (`GET /api/chats/page`), only in
`GET /api/chats/page?archived=true`; it is unpinned. A new message brings it back, unless
the chat is muted. The caller's other devices get `ChatStateChanged`.
            
Errors: `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`.
put.summary: Move a chat to the archive, or back.

get.description:
For the owner and admins. Newest first; `nextCursor` — pass it as `cursor` for
older entries. Actions: `group_created`, `title_changed`,
`member_permissions_changed`, `members_added`, `member_removed`,
`member_left`, `role_changed`, `permissions_changed`,
`ownership_transferred`, `message_deleted` (someone else's message deleted by an
admin); `data` holds the details.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `400 INVALID_CURSOR`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`,
`403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (not an admin).

parameters.description: From the previous page; omit for the newest.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: The group's action log.

delete.description:
Like setting one: `changeInfo`, a system message (`photo_removed`), `ChatUpdated`
with `avatarId: null`.

put.description:
A photo the caller uploaded (`POST /api/media/uploads`, kind `photo`). Needs the
`changeInfo` permission. Members get a system message (`photo_changed`) and
`ChatUpdated` with `avatarId`; the same photo again changes nothing.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `400 INVALID_AVATAR` (not a photo), `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`,
`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, `404 ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`.

delete.description:
The user's devices receive `DraftUpdated` with `draft: null`. Without a draft —
`204` and no event. Errors: `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
delete.summary: Remove the draft of this chat.

put.description:
One draft per user and chat, shared by the user's devices: they receive `DraftUpdated`,
and a new device finds the draft in `GET /api/chats` (`draft`). Save with a pause
of a second or two after typing stops, not on every key. The text is kept as typed (not
trimmed); formatting and the reply follow the rules of sending. Text of only spaces without
a reply removes the draft — `204`. Sending a message to the chat removes it too.
The same draft again changes nothing and sends nothing.
            
Errors: `400 MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`, `400 INVALID_ENTITIES`, `400 REPLY_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`,
`403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
put.summary: Save the draft of this chat.

get.description:
Returns the same `ChatListItemDto` as one entry of `GET /api/chats`,
resolved for the caller: companion id/name/username for private chats,
unread count and last message preview.
            
Purpose: the client knows only a `chatId` (after a push, a deep link,
or a `ChatListUpdated` event) and needs to render or refresh exactly
one row without refetching the whole list.
            
Use `GET /api/chats/{chatId}` instead when you need the participant list.
get.summary: Get a single chat in chat-list shape.

put.description:
A reminder for the user only: nobody else sees it, the unread counter does not change.
Reading the chat (`POST /read`) removes it. The caller's devices receive
`ReadStateChanged`; setting what is already set changes nothing and sends nothing.
            
Errors: `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
put.summary: Mark the chat as unread, or remove the mark.

get.description:
Messages of the chat that carry files of the kind (`media` — photos and videos,
`files`, `voice`) or web links (`links` — an address in the text or a link in
the formatting), **newest first**, as a gallery shows them. The same `MessageDto` as the
history, with `attachments`; previews come from `POST /api/media/links`. What the
caller deleted for themselves is left out.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_FILTER`, `400 INVALID_CURSOR`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`.

parameters.description: From the previous page; omit for the newest.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: The chat's gallery: photos and videos, files, voice messages or links.

get.description:
Owner first, then admins, then members by joining time. `permissions` is what the member
may do now: the role, the group's defaults and their own overrides together.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`.
get.summary: Members of a group with their roles and permissions.

post.description:
Needs `addMembers`. Those already in the group are skipped; the body lists who was
added (empty — nobody new). New members see the whole history, but only what comes after
joining counts as unread; they receive `ChatCreated`. The members already there receive
`MemberAdded` and a system message "members added".
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (nobody besides the caller),
`400 TOO_MANY_MEMBERS`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`,
`404 USER_NOT_FOUND`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

delete.description:
Another member — the owner removes anyone, an admin with `removeMembers` — members only.
Oneself — leaving: the owner hands the group over to the longest-standing admin (or member),
the last member deletes it. The removed one loses the chat with its history.
            
Everyone, the removed one included, receives `MemberRemoved`; the rest also get a system
message. The removed one's connections stop getting the chat's events.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`,
`404 MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

parameters.description: The member; the caller's own id — leave
parameters.name: userId

delete.summary: Remove a member, or leave the group.

put.description:
Replaces the member's overrides: a given field overrides the role and the group's defaults,
an omitted one follows them (`{}` removes all overrides). For a member — the owner or an
admin with `removeMembers`, and only `sendMessages`, `sendMedia`,
`addMembers`, `changeInfo`; for an admin — the owner, any permission. Members receive
`MemberUpdated`.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `400 INVALID_PERMISSIONS` (an admin permission for a member),
`403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, `404 MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`,
`429 RATE_LIMITED`.

schema.description: A change of permissions: only the given fields change, the others stay as they are.
A change of permissions: only the given fields change, the others stay as they are.
A change of permissions: only the given fields change, the others stay as they are.

put.description:
- `admin` — make a member an admin: the owner, or an admin with `addAdmins`.
- `member` — make an admin a member again: the owner.
- `owner` — hand the group over: the owner; they become an admin.
            
A new role starts without the member's own permission overrides. Members receive
`MemberUpdated` (for a handover — about both). The same role again changes nothing.
            
Errors: `400 NOT_A_GROUP`, `400 INVALID_ROLE`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`,
`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, `404 MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
put.summary: Change a member's role, or hand the group over.

post.description:
Same rules and events as the hub method `SendMessage`: the text is trimmed
and must be 1–4096 characters; chat members receive `MessageCreated` and
`ChatListUpdated` over SignalR, the sender included — other devices of the
sender learn about the message the same way.
            
Pass a fresh `clientMessageId` with every message and repeat it on retries:
a retry returns the already created message with `200` instead of `201`
and sends no events.
            
Errors: `400 MESSAGE_EMPTY`, `400 MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`,
`403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `409 CLIENT_MESSAGE_ID_CONFLICT` (the id is taken
by a message in another chat), `429 RATE_LIMITED` (commands limit per user).

get.description:
Returns a page of messages cursor-based, with the most recent message at or before
the given date as the last item in the page.
Use the returned `nextCursor` to scroll further back.

Purpose: "Jump to March 15", "Open chat where I left off", "Go to unread messages".

parameters.description: Target date (ISO 8601). Finds messages at or before this date.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Number of messages per page (default 20, max 100).
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Get messages around a specific date.

get.description:
Returns messages ordered chronologically (oldest first).
Use the `cursor` parameter from the previous response's `nextCursor` field
to fetch the next (older) page. When `cursor` is omitted, returns the most recent messages.

The response includes:
- `items`: the messages in this page
- `nextCursor`: pass this as `cursor` to get the next page (null = no more pages)
- `hasMore`: whether more messages exist beyond this page

parameters.description: Cursor from previous response (optional). Omit for the first page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Number of messages per page (default 20, max 100).
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Get messages with cursor-based pagination.

post.description:
Copies 1–100 messages of `fromChatId` into this chat in their original order.
Each copy is a new message of the caller with `forwardFrom` — the original
author (for a forward of a forward — the very first one). Replies are not carried over.
Members of this chat receive `MessageCreated` and `ChatListUpdated` for each copy.
            
Pass `clientMessageIds` (one per message, same order) and repeat them on retries:
a retry creates nothing new and answers `200` instead of `201`.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (empty or repeated ids, `clientMessageIds` of another
length), `400 TOO_MANY_MESSAGES`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER` (of either chat),
`404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` (a message is not in `fromChatId`, deleted or hidden by
the caller), `409 CLIENT_MESSAGE_ID_CONFLICT`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
post.summary: Forward messages from another chat (or this one).

get.description:
Searches messages by text content using PostgreSQL full-text search.
Returns messages ordered chronologically (oldest first, newest matches).
Supports cursor-based pagination — use the returned `nextCursor` to fetch older results.

The response includes:
- `items`: matching messages with sender names
- `nextCursor`: pass this as `cursor` to get the next page (null = no more pages)
- `hasMore`: whether more matches exist beyond this page
- `query`: the original search query
- `totalCount`: total number of matches for this query

parameters.description: Number of results per page (default 20, max 100).
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Full-text search for messages within a chat.

delete.description:
`forEveryone=true` — only the author, within `Messages:DeleteWindowHours`
             (48 by default). The message disappears from history, search and the chat list for
             all members; they receive `MessageDeleted` with `forEveryone: true`.
            
             Without it — any member, any message, any time: the message disappears only for the
             caller; their devices receive `MessageDeleted` with `forEveryone: false`.
            
             Repeating a delete returns `204` and sends nothing.
            
             Errors: `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `403 NOT_MESSAGE_AUTHOR`,
             `403 DELETE_WINDOW_EXPIRED`, `404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

parameters.description: Delete for all members, not only for yourself.
parameters.name: forEveryone

delete.summary: Delete a message for everyone or only for yourself.

patch.description:
Only the author, within `Messages:EditWindowHours` (48 by default) of sending.
The text follows the same rules as when sending. Members receive `MessageUpdated`
with the whole message; `editedAt` is set. The same text again changes nothing
and sends no event.
            
Errors: `400 MESSAGE_EMPTY`, `400 MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`,
`403 NOT_MESSAGE_AUTHOR`, `403 EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED`,
`404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` (not in this chat or deleted), `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

delete.description:
Members receive `ReactionsChanged` with `emoji: null`. Without a reaction —
`204` and no event. Errors as for putting one.
delete.summary: Remove your reaction from a message.

put.description:
One reaction per user per message: a new one replaces the previous. The emoji must be one
of the instance's set (`Messages:Reactions`). Members receive `ReactionsChanged`;
the same reaction again changes nothing and sends no event.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_REACTION`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`,
`404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` (not in this chat, deleted, or hidden by the caller),
`429 RATE_LIMITED`.
put.summary: Put a reaction on a message.

put.description:
`{ "muted": true, "until": "…" }` — until the moment; without `until` — for good;
             `{ "muted": false }` — unmute. A muted chat sends no notifications and does not leave the
             archive on a new message; the unread counter works as usual. The caller's other devices get
             `ChatStateChanged`.
            
             Errors: `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (`until` in the past), `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`.
put.summary: Mute a chat, or unmute it.

put.description:
A newly pinned chat goes on top; at most 10 are pinned. A pinned chat leaves the archive.
Answers with the pinned chats, top first; the caller's other devices get
`PinnedChatsChanged` with the same list.
            
Errors: `400 TOO_MANY_PINNED`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`.
put.summary: Pin a chat on top of the list, or unpin it.

post.description:
Moves the caller's read pointer to this message (forward only; an older one is not an
error) and clears "marked as unread". Authors whose messages first became read receive
`MessagesRead`; the caller's devices receive `ReadStateChanged` with the new counters.
            
Errors: `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`, `404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` (not in this chat).

Same as the hub method `Typing`: other members receive `TypingChanged`.
"Typing" expires after 6 seconds unless repeated, so send `isTyping: true`
every few seconds while the user types and `false` when they stop.

get.description:
A device is one sign-in (login or registration) with the token refreshes after it; it is gone
after logout, when its refresh token expires or when it is signed out from another device.
`isCurrent` marks the one the request came from.
get.summary: The caller's devices: every sign-in that is still open.

delete.description:
Its refresh token stops working and its hub connections close at once; an access token it
already holds works until it expires (minutes). The current device may be signed out too —
the same as logout.
            
Errors: `404 DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` — not the caller's or already signed out.

parameters.description: The device id from the list.
parameters.name: deviceId

get.summary: The caller's folders, in their order.

post.description:
A folder shows the chats listed in `chatIds` and, by filters, all private chats
(`includePrivate`) or all groups (`includeGroups`) outside the archive; with
`onlyUnread` — only those with something unread. `pinnedChatIds` — pinned inside
the folder, top first (they are in the folder too). Up to 20 folders, 200 listed and 10 pinned
chats in each; the new folder goes last. The caller's devices get `FoldersChanged` with
all folders.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_TITLE` (1–64 characters), `400 TOO_MANY_FOLDERS`,
`400 INVALID_REQUEST` (limits; a chat the caller is not in).

schema.description: A new folder, or changes to one: a null field stays as it is.
A new folder, or changes to one: a null field stays as it is.
A new folder, or changes to one: a null field stays as it is.

put.summary: Reorder the folders: exactly the caller's folders, in the new order.

delete.summary: Delete a folder; its chats stay where they are.

patch.description: Errors: as for creation, and `404 FOLDER_NOT_FOUND`.

schema.description: A new folder, or changes to one: a null field stays as it is.
A new folder, or changes to one: a null field stays as it is.
A new folder, or changes to one: a null field stays as it is.

patch.summary: Change a folder: only the fields given (lists are replaced whole).

get.description:
The same `ChatListItemDto` as `GET /api/chats/page`: the first page starts with the
chats pinned in the folder (outside the limit), then the others by activity.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_CURSOR`, `404 FOLDER_NOT_FOUND`.
get.summary: The folder's chats, a page at a time.

post.description:
Up to 100 ids at once — a screen of previews in one request. Files the caller may not see are
left out of the answer. Links are signed and work for `Media:DownloadUrlMinutes` (60)
minutes. Photos, videos and voice are served for display; other files only as a download of
unknown type.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

schema.description: What the client is about to upload.
What the client is about to upload.
What the client is about to upload.

post.description:
The server reads what was uploaded: the real size, the SHA-256, the type by content. A photo
must be a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP picture — the server measures it and makes a preview; a video
must be MP4, MOV or WebM, a voice message Ogg, WebM, MP4 or MP3. A file that fails the check is
removed. Repeating the call returns the same file.
            
Errors: `400 UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` — nothing was put at the link yet,
`400 FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `400 INVALID_MEDIA`, `404 UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` — no such
upload of the caller (or it went stale and was removed).
post.summary: Finish an upload: the server checks the file and makes it usable.

get.description: `302` to a signed link — for code that downloads with the access token. For `` use links from `POST /api/media/links`: a browser does not send the token with a picture request. Errors: `404 ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND` — no such file, the caller may not see it, or (for the file itself) it has expired.
get.summary: Redirect to a file (or its preview).

get.description: Pass `vapidPublicKey` as `applicationServerKey` to `pushManager.subscribe`.
get.summary: Whether the server sends push notifications, and its key to subscribe with.

delete.summary: Stop push notifications to this device.

put.description:
The body is the browser's `PushSubscription.toJSON()`. One subscription per device (the
sign-in the token belongs to): a new one replaces the old. A subscription the same browser
gave another sign-in — for instance, before logging in as someone else — moves to this one.
Logout and signing the device out remove it. Only push services the server knows are taken:
Google (Chrome), Mozilla, Microsoft (Edge) and Apple (Safari) by default.
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_SUBSCRIPTION`, `404 DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` (the sign-in has already
ended), `503 PUSH_UNAVAILABLE` (push is off on this server).

schema.description: A browser push subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives it.
A browser push subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives it.
A browser push subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives it.

put.summary: Subscribe this device to push notifications.

get.description:
The same full-text search as in a chat (Russian morphology, words as prefixes), over every
chat the caller is in now. Deleted messages, the caller's hidden ones and system messages are
not found. Newest first; `nextCursor` — for the next page. Each hit is the message
(`MessageDto`) and its chat: type, title or companion, avatar.
            
Filters: `chatId`, `senderId`, `from`/`to` (the time, `to` exclusive),
`type` — `text` or `media` (the caption is searched).
            
Errors: `400 INVALID_QUERY` (shorter than 2 characters), `400 INVALID_FILTER`,
`400 INVALID_CURSOR`, `403 NOT_A_MEMBER` (a chat filter for a chat the caller is not in).
get.summary: Search messages across all the caller's chats.

get.description:
After a reconnect: apply `updates` in order (each has the same payload as the
hub event of the same name), store the returned `pts`, repeat while
`hasMore`. An update may also have arrived over the hub — recognize it by
the message or chat id.
            
`snapshotRequired: true` — the journal no longer reaches back to
`since` (kept for 30 days): take `GET /api/sync/state` instead.

parameters.description: The last pts the client knows (0 — nothing yet).
parameters.name: since

get.summary: Updates after `since`, in order.

post.description:
The device is the sign-in behind the access token. The acknowledged pts only moves
forward. New messages the journal carried up to this pts become `delivered`: their
authors get `MessagesDelivered` if no other member had received them before.
post.summary: Confirm that this device has received updates up to `pts`.

get.description:
Call on first start and whenever `GET /api/sync` answers
`snapshotRequired: true`. Keep `pts`: it is the `since` of the next
`GET /api/sync`.
get.summary: Snapshot to start from: the chat list and the current `pts`.
